contribution.value: QuaRot is a rotation-based PTQ scheme that fuses randomized Hadamard transforms into LLM weights to eliminate activation outliers, enabling end-to-end 4-bit quantization of weights, activations, and KV cache with minimal accuracy loss.

ev.quote: We introduce QuaRot, a new Quantization scheme based on Rotations, which is able to quantize LLMs end-to-end, including all weights, activations, and KV cache in 4 bits. QuaRot rotates LLMs in a way that removes outliers from the hidden state without changing the output, making quantization easier.
We use 128 samples from WikiText-2 [Merity et al., 2016] training set with 2048 sequence length as the calibration set during GPTQ quantization

strengths.value: First end-to-end 4-bit scheme that quantizes weights, activations, and KV cache without keeping outlier channels in higher precision.

ev.quote: QuaRot: a method which uses Hadamard matrices to eliminate outliers in the activations and KV cache of pre-trained LLMs, enabling end-to-end 4-bit quantization for the first time

strengths.value: Strong accuracy retention: LLaMA-2-70B at 4-bit loses at most 0.47 PPL on WikiText-2 and keeps 99% of zero-shot accuracy.

ev.quote: Our 4-bit quantized LLAMA2-70B model has losses of at most 0.47 WikiText-2 perplexity and retains 99% of the zero-shot performance

strengths.value: Real consumer-GPU speedups: up to 3.33x prefill speedup on LLaMA-2-70B and up to 3.89x decoding memory saving on RTX 3090.

ev.quote: QuaRot achieves up to 3.33x prefill speedups (on a batch size 64 with 2048 sequence length), and 3.89x memory saving during the decoding stage

strengths.value: Lossless 6- and 8-bit quantization without any calibration data, using simple round-to-nearest weight quantization.

ev.quote: QuaRot can provide lossless 6 and 8 bit LLAMA-2 models without any calibration data using round-to-nearest quantization

weaknesses.value: 4-bit RTN weight quantization shows a large gap to GPTQ on small models (LLaMA-2-7B PPL rises from 6.10 to 8.37).

ev.quote: in 4 bits, the gap between QuaRot-RTN and QuaRot-GPTQ decreases when the model size is increased (2.27 on LLAMA2-7B and 0.34 on LLAMA2-70B )

weaknesses.value: 4-bit KV cache offers no decoding speedup at small batch sizes (<=8); benefit only appears at large batch or long sequence.

ev.quote: The 4-bit cache is slower than FP16 for smaller batch sizes (e.g. up to 8). Note that this is intuitive as the main benefit of the 4-bit cache is reducing the I/O cost

weaknesses.value: LLaMA-3 is more sensitive to 4-bit quantization than LLaMA-2, with larger PPL gaps to FP16 (8.16 vs 6.14 on LLaMA-3-8B).

ev.quote: we conclude that LLAMA-3 is more sensitive to quantization as we can see a higher gap between the quantized and FP16 models

weaknesses.value: Performance results measured on a single transformer block since the full model does not fit on the GPU cluster used.

ev.quote: We provide all our experiments on a single transformer block as the whole model does not fit on our GPU cluster for large batch sizes

limitations.value: Residual stream is not quantized; future work to extend QuaRot to quantize residuals and mixture-of-experts.

ev.quote: Opportunities to build on QuaRot include quantizing the residuals and extending the method to mixture-of-experts architectures

limitations.value: Safety, jailbreak, bias, or refusal behaviour after 4-bit quantization is not evaluated, only perplexity and zero-shot.

ev.quote: we focus on evaluating QuaRot on six important zero-shot tasks: PIQA, WinoGrande, HellaSwag, LAMBADA (OpenAI), and Arc (Easy and Challenge)

limitations.value: No edge or mobile hardware tested; speedups are reported only on RTX 3090 and A100 data-centre GPUs.

ev.quote: we evaluate all the performance experiments on NVIDIA RTX 3090 GPUs

limitations.value: Long-context (>=8K) behaviour is not evaluated; experiments use 2048-token sequences.

ev.quote: Left: For the speedup results, we evaluate using sequence length 2048 with different batch sizes

future_work_stated.value: Quantize the residual stream and extend QuaRot to mixture-of-experts architectures.

ev.quote: Opportunities to build on QuaRot include quantizing the residuals and extending the method to mixture-of-experts architectures

future_work_stated.value: Exploit upcoming INT4 hardware (e.g. NVIDIA B200) to deliver speedups similar to FP4 at lower implementation cost.

ev.quote: end-to-end INT4 inference with QuaRot could be exploited to give similar speedups as that of the recently announced NVIDIA B200 GPU architecture, while being much cheaper to implement compared to the floating point (FP4) format

future_work_stated.value: Optimize the kernels further by fusing quantization operations into the matrix multiplication.

ev.quote: our performance results could be improved by optimizing our kernels (e.g., fusing the quantization operations into the MatMul)
